web.aboutTitle: Every puzzle brings your world to life.
web.story: A supply run takes an unexpected turn when you follow a beacon from a lost expedition. After an emergency landing, the journey starts with a damaged ship — and one small repair.
web.aboutBody: Solve match-3 puzzles to restore each section, uncover the ship’s log, and set a course for distant worlds. Watch places change as you progress, one repair at a time.
web.tileNote: Make a match. Make a difference.
web.repairBody: From the first flicker of light to a ship ready for the stars.
web.iceAlt: An expedition to an icy world
web.exploreBody: Travel beyond the crash site and uncover the expedition’s trail.
web.restoreBody: Discover new places, new puzzles, and something worth restoring.
web.guidesTitle: A little help along the way.
web.guideMatch: Swap neighbouring tiles to match at least three of the same type. Check the goals above the board: some levels need specific colours, covers or charged rings. Complete every goal before running out of moves.
web.guideStars: Winning unlocks the next task. Three stars are an optional challenge; you can replay completed repairs through Chapters.
web.guideCharges: Match four in a line or five in a T or L to create Pulse, which hits a 3×3 area. Five or more in a line create Nova, which hits a row and column. Tap a charge to fire it for one move; chain reactions are free. You can also drag a charge to a neighbour if the other tile forms a valid match: one move, without firing.
web.guideTools: Tools below the board spend stock instead of moves. Laser hits one tile, Shuffle rearranges tiles, Swap exchanges neighbours, Beam hits a row and EMP hits a 3×3 area. Use ⓘ in a puzzle to reopen the illustrated help.
web.guideCovers: A covered tile cannot be moved. Include it in a match to break its cover; the tile stays for another match. Blasts can also break covers.
web.guideRings: Charge rings by making matches directly beside them: above, below, left or right. Each separate match adds one charge per ring, even in the same wave. Diagonal matches and direct blasts do not charge rings.
web.guideEnergy: The first valid move reserves one energy charge. Winning returns it; losing, leaving after a move or refreshing keeps the charge spent. Opening a puzzle without making a move costs no energy. The energy display shows when a charge will return.
web.guideSave: Guest progress is saved in this browser. Sign in with Google for cloud progress on the same account across devices. Energy and tool stock are stored locally.
web.guideTransfer: Played on the original address? Transfer your saved game first, then sign in with the same Google account on the new address. Signing in alone does not transfer local energy and tools. The original save remains available.
news.answer-200.title: The journey reaches level 200.
news.answer-200.body: The Answer adds thirteen puzzles across three beacon links and the central rescue station. Restore the connections and bring this journey after the signal to its conclusion. The adventure now includes 200 levels.
news.display-update.title: More room for your next move.
news.display-update.body: Puzzle boards now make better use of small phones and larger displays. Result screens and controls are clearer, and touch phones show a rotate prompt when held sideways. Later levels have received targeted difficulty adjustments.
news.archive-of-echoes.title: The Archive of Echoes awaits.
news.archive-of-echoes.body: The story continues through the Arrival Dock and the Archive of Echoes. Explore four archive areas, restore their systems and uncover the history behind the signal. The released adventure now includes 187 levels.
news.language-review.title: Clearer words. A smoother journey.
news.language-review.body: English and Czech text has been reviewed throughout the game. Puzzle tips and instructions are clearer, with improved readability on small screens. Level difficulty is unchanged.
news.first-playtest.title: A fresh pair of eyes on the adventure.
news.first-playtest.body: Our first Bounty Board playtest is underway. New players are exploring the opening, trying the puzzles, and sharing honest feedback to help us improve the experience.

web.about.title: A small repair. A much bigger journey.
web.about.description: Discover the story, puzzles and changing worlds of Beyond the Signal, an independent browser game with 200 levels.
web.about.intro: Beyond the Signal is a free sci-fi match-3 adventure. Every completed puzzle restores something in the world: a damaged ship, an abandoned installation or a place that still has a future.
web.about.adventure.title: Follow a signal that should not be there
web.about.adventure.body: You are the pilot of a supply ship. A beacon from a lost expedition draws you off course; an emergency landing leaves your ship badly damaged. The first task is simple: get one system working again. Repairs uncover the ship’s log and gradually turn survival into a journey after the signal.
web.about.adventure.extra: The released adventure contains 200 levels. It begins aboard your ship and continues through distant worlds, stations and the traces of the missing expedition. You can read the optional story entries at your own pace; solving the puzzles moves the journey forward.
web.about.changes.title: Puzzles with a visible result
web.about.changes.body: Match neighbouring tiles to meet the goals within a move limit. Later puzzles introduce protective covers, resonators and charges that can clear several tiles at once. The reward is a direct change to the scene around you. Repairs do not require a separate currency or a resource shop.
web.about.changes.extra: Winning is enough to continue. Three-star results are an optional challenge, and completed puzzles can be revisited through Chapters. The game runs in mobile and desktop browsers without installation. On touch phones, play in portrait orientation.
web.about.creator.title: An independent game, still growing
web.about.creator.body: Beyond the Signal is created and operated by Michal Malich. Updates and player feedback help shape the adventure, its readability and its puzzle balance. The updates page records released changes; guides explain the current rules. For a problem report, include your device, browser, language and the level or place where it happened.
web.basics.title: Your first moves in Beyond the Signal
web.basics.description: Learn how to swap tiles, read puzzle goals, manage moves and replay levels for stars in Beyond the Signal.
web.basics.intro: You do not need to memorise every mechanic before you begin. Start with the goals above the board, then look for a useful match. This guide explains the rules that stay with you throughout the journey.
web.basics.controls.title: 1. Swap two neighbours
web.basics.controls.body: Tap or click one tile and then a neighbouring tile, or drag it towards its neighbour. Ordinary tiles swap when the move creates a horizontal or vertical line of at least three identical tiles. A diagonal line does not count. An invalid swap does not use a move. Wait for the falling tiles and any cascades to settle before choosing the next action.
web.basics.goals.title: 2. Read every goal above the board
web.basics.goals.body: Some puzzles ask for a total number of tiles; others need particular colours or several goals at once. A match in another colour can still rearrange the board, but it will not complete a colour goal. If the level includes covers or resonators, those also need to be finished. Empty spaces in a shaped board are not tiles.
web.basics.moves.title: 3. Make the limited moves count
web.basics.moves.body: A valid swap or a tap that fires a charge uses one move. Cascades and chained blasts do not cost additional moves. Tools below the board use their own stock instead of a move. The final move is evaluated after its cascades finish, so a last-move success still wins the puzzle.
web.basics.stars.title: 4. A win opens the way; stars are optional
web.basics.stars.body: Complete all goals to unlock the next task and its repair. Stars reflect how many moves remain from the original limit: at least 30% for three stars, at least 15% for two, otherwise one. Thresholds round up to whole moves; bonus moves do not increase this rating. Open Chapters, visit the room and choose a completed repair to replay it. Your best star result is kept.
web.basics.stuck.title: When the next move is hard to see
web.basics.stuck.body: Each attempt offers one free hint. Use the ⓘ button to reopen illustrated explanations of the mechanics and tools. If a board has no legal action, the game attempts to restore a playable arrangement without spending a move. Before spending a tool, check which goal is actually holding you back.
web.mechanics.title: Charges, tools and the obstacles in your way
web.mechanics.description: Understand Pulse and Nova, legal charge swaps, tools, protective covers, resonators and cascade rewards.
web.mechanics.intro: Charges are pieces you create on the board. Tools are the limited supplies below it. Knowing the difference helps you choose what to use and when.
web.mechanics.charges.title: Create and fire Pulse or Nova
web.mechanics.charges.body: Four matching tiles in a line, or five arranged in a T or L, create Pulse. Tap it to hit a 3×3 area. A line of five or more creates Nova, which hits its row and column. Firing either charge costs one move. Charges caught in another blast fire for free, allowing a chain reaction.
web.mechanics.moving.title: Move a charge only with a valid match
web.mechanics.moving.body: You can drag a charge into a neighbouring position if the ordinary tile moving the other way forms a valid match. This costs one move and does not fire the charge. A swap that only changes the charge’s position without making that match is rejected. Tap the charge when you want to fire it where it currently stands.
web.mechanics.tools.title: Tools spend stock, not moves
web.mechanics.tools.body: Laser hits one selected tile. Shuffle rearranges uncovered tiles. Swap exchanges two uncovered neighbours even without a match. Beam hits a selected row, and EMP hits a 3×3 area around a selected tile. Each use spends one item from the corresponding stock. Select the tool, then its target; Shuffle acts immediately. A tool’s blast can also activate a charge.
web.mechanics.covers.title: A cover breaks before its tile is collected
web.mechanics.covers.body: The tile under a protective cover is visible but cannot be swapped. Include it in a match of the same type to break the cover. The tile stays on the board and can be collected in a later match. A neighbouring match alone is not enough. Blasts also break covers; a covered tile struck by a tool loses its cover first.
web.mechanics.rings.title: Resonators need adjacent matches
web.mechanics.rings.body: A matched tile must touch a ring directly above, below, left or right. Each separate matching combination adds one charge to every ring it touches. Two independent combinations in the same wave can therefore add two charges to one ring. A connected T or L counts as one combination. Diagonal contact and direct blasts do not charge rings. Each ring shows its current charge and target.
web.mechanics.cascades.title: A long cascade can leave a bonus Pulse
web.mechanics.cascades.body: Three further matching cascades after the initial action can award one bonus Pulse on the board. It appears after the cascades settle, at most once per move; it does not fire automatically or enter your tool stock. Tap it later for one move. Tool actions do not award this bonus, and an already won puzzle does not need another charge.
web.saving.title: Keep your progress, energy and tools
web.saving.description: How browser saves, Google cloud progress, energy and the move to game.playbeyondthesignal.com work in Beyond the Signal.
web.saving.intro: Progress and supplies do not all live in the same place. Read this before moving to another browser or device, clearing browsing data, or transferring from the original address.
web.saving.guest.title: Guest play stays in this browser
web.saving.guest.body: You can play without signing in. Completed repairs, chapters, stars and read story entries are saved locally. Return using the same address, browser and browser profile to find that save. A private window has separate storage, which may disappear when it closes. An unfinished puzzle board is not restored after refreshing.
web.saving.account.title: Google sign-in carries cloud progress
web.saving.account.body: In Settings, sign in with Google to save account progress online. Use the same Google account on another device. The game shows whether progress is saved online or only locally while the cloud is unavailable. Signing in is separate on the original domain and game. If you first played as a guest, the settings offer an explicit import of that browser’s guest progress into the account.
web.saving.local.title: Energy and tools remain local
web.saving.local.body: Google sign-in does not synchronise energy or tool stock between devices. There are up to five energy charges. The first valid action in a puzzle reserves one; winning returns it. Losing, leaving after an action or refreshing a started attempt keeps it spent. Before the first ship departure, one charge returns every 10 minutes; afterwards, every 30 minutes. The in-game countdown shows your next recharge.
web.saving.transfer.title: Moving from the original address to game.
web.saving.transfer.body: Use Transfer my saved game before starting a new save on game. Open the original saved game in the browser where you used to play, send the copy and confirm the import on the new address. This includes local energy and tools as well as saved progress. The original copy is kept. Then continue to the game and sign in again with the same Google account if you used one before. Guests can continue without signing in.
web.saving.transfer.extra: If the popup is blocked, the transfer pages also offer a downloadable JSON backup and file import. Close other game tabs on the destination before importing. Review any conflicting saved data before choosing which copy to keep. Repeating the same transfer does not refill spent energy or tools.
web.saving.recovery.title: If progress seems to be missing
web.saving.recovery.body: Check the address, browser profile and Google account first. Do not reset the game or clear storage while looking for an older save. For missing local supplies after moving domains, use the original-save transfer rather than signing in repeatedly. If the original browser data has already been deleted, its local energy and tools cannot be recovered from Google cloud progress. Contact support with the affected device and account email; never send authentication tokens.
web.saving.privacy.title: Statistics are your choice
web.saving.privacy.body: The first visit offers a choice about sharing gameplay statistics. You can change it later in Settings, and declining does not limit play or cloud saving. Advertising privacy choices are separate. The privacy page explains the stored information, providers and deletion options.
web.updates.title: Updates from beyond the signal
web.updates.description: Released chapters, improvements and development updates for Beyond the Signal.
web.updates.intro: Follow released changes and clearly marked development news: new places to restore, clearer controls and improvements informed by player feedback. Features still in development are described separately from updates you can play today.

news.challenge-and-replay.title: A tighter challenge, with room to try again.
news.challenge-and-replay.body: We have reduced move limits in 33 selected levels from level 20 onwards, including several HARD challenges. Completed ship sections can be replayed before departure, so you can practise and improve your stars. Undo now prepares your available use first; a second tap returns the move. Your progress and earned stars are preserved.
news.android-preview.title: The Android app is being tested.
news.android-preview.body: An Android version of Beyond the Signal is now in internal testing on a real phone. We are checking controls, saved progress and rewarded ads before a wider release. The app is not yet publicly available to download or on Google Play. You can keep playing all 200 levels in your browser.
